title: What Is Bloomscrolling? How to Make Social Media Work for Your Mental Health
summary: Bloomscrolling means choosing uplifting content on purpose. Learn what it is, what research says, and simple examples to help your feed support your mental health.
body_markdown:
## Bloomscrolling Examples and How to Start


Bloomscrolling tends to work best when it is built into the feed itself. A few ideas to try:


#### Follow Your Favorite Hobbies


Follow accounts tied to things you already love, such as gardening, baking, knitting, woodworking, running, or birdwatching. Hobby content tends to feel calm and doable, and it can nudge people to put the phone down and try something themselves. Slow, low-pressure pastimes, sometimes called[cozy hobbies](https://lifestance.com/blog/cozy-hobbies-for-mental-health/) , may be especially soothing.


#### Good News in Your Community


Follow local libraries, parks, farmers’ markets, animal shelters, schools, and community groups. Their posts often highlight neighbors helping neighbors, upcoming events, and small wins that make a place feel like home.


#### Curate Your Social Media Feed Carefully


Most apps learn from what people engage with, so small choices add up. Try these steps:


- Unfollow or mute accounts that leave you feeling anxious, angry, or not good enough
- Notice content that pulls you into[comparing yourself to others](https://lifestance.com/blog/feeling-behind-in-life/) and scroll past it
- Use “not interested” or similar tools to tell the app what you would rather not see
- Save, like, and share the posts you want to see more of


#### Nature, Animals, and Wholesome Content


Nature scenes, animal videos, and simple wholesome content – a sunrise, a toddler’s first steps, a cat napping in a sunbeam – are classic bloomscrolling picks. They can also be a gentle reminder to look for the same comfort offline, from the[benefits of nature](https://lifestance.com/blog/benefits-of-nature-on-mental-health/) to the bond between[pets and mental health](https://lifestance.com/blog/pets-and-mental-health-benefits/) .


#### Learn Something New


Short lessons on cooking, history, a new language, science, or art can turn idle scrolling into something that feels worthwhile. When the topic is health, be sure to look for information shared by credentialed professionals.


#### Creators Who Share Kindness


Some creators build their whole feed around good deeds, gratitude, and everyday kindness. Pairing that content with a small daily habit, like taking a moment to[practice gratitude](https://lifestance.com/blog/how-to-practice-gratitude-daily/) , may help the good feeling last beyond the screen.


#### Keep Bloomscrolling in Balance


Even with uplifting content, boundaries are important. A few habits can help:


- Pause every 5 to 10 minutes and check in with how you feel – if your mood is dropping, it is time to stop
- Turn off news alerts so headlines do not pull you back in
- Set a daily time limit, since even good content can crowd out sleep, movement, and time with people
- Keep the phone off the nightstand at night
- Take it offline: try the recipe, visit the park, or call the friend


For a bigger reset, a short[digital detox](https://lifestance.com/blog/how-to-do-digital-detox-advice-from-expert/) may also help.
